data.help: How many bots each band holds and what they are built from: the rating window they spread across, the level they show, and the champions and relics their defence is synthesised at. The ladder must never be empty — a new account has to find somebody to fight on its first evening. Sixty by default, weighted to the bottom (ECONOMY_BALANCE §12).
data.label: Bot ladder recipes

data.help: The second half of a bot’s name. Keep them ≤8 characters: a profile name is at most sixteen, and a name that will not fit is a bot that cannot be created.
data.label: Bot names — epithets

data.help: The first half of a bot’s name. Multiplied by the epithet list, so adding one word here adds a name for every epithet. Natural names with no bot marker, by the owner’s decision (GAME_DESIGN §9.3) — keep them ≤7 characters so every combination fits a profile name.
data.label: Bot names — given

data.help: A loss inside Bronze cannot drop a rating below its tier floor. A friendlier smalltown ladder than the source game’s — a new account should not be able to fall out of the bottom.
data.label: Bronze loss protection

data.help: After these, a refresh costs crystals. Resets on the daily reset hour with every other allowance.
data.label: Free offer refreshes per day

data.help: Medals for each level of one track, 1 → 10. Twenty-four tracks at ~2,500 each is a year-scale sink by design.
data.label: Hall of Valor level costs

data.help: What one level of a track gives: a percentage for HP/ATK/DEF/C.DMG, flat points for ACC/RES.
data.label: Hall of Valor per level

data.help: By band. The only faucet for the Hall of Valor besides the weekly chest.
data.label: Valor Medals per win

data.help: How many opponents the hub shows at once.
data.label: Opponents on offer

data.help: How far one result can move a rating. Elo-lite: the swing shrinks as the gap between the two ratings grows.
data.label: Rating K-factor

data.help: Crystals for a refresh once the free ones are gone.
data.label: Paid offer refresh

data.help: Where a new account joins the ladder — inside Bronze II, so the first win is a promotion rather than a rounding error.
data.label: Starting rating

data.help: Rating at which each rung of the ladder begins. Where the rungs sit is the main lever on how a season feels (ECONOMY_BALANCE §8).
data.label: Tier thresholds

data.help: Tokens accrue to this and stop. Source-faithful.
data.label: Attack token cap

data.help: Seconds per token. Derived from the clock like energy — there is no ticking job to fall behind.
data.label: Attack token regen

data.help: Paid against the best tier held during the week, not the tier held on Monday morning — falling out of Gold on Sunday evening must not cost a week of Gold.
data.label: Weekly tier chest

data.help: Percentage of the distance from the current rating down to its tier floor, shed at the Monday reset. Keeps an abandoned account from holding a Platinum slot forever without resetting anybody to zero.
data.label: Weekly rating decay

data.help: Each ascension level adds this percentage to HP, ATK and DEF.
data.label: Ascension bonus per level

data.help: Primary stats scale as (level / 60) ^ exponent, then blend with the level-1 floor. Higher means more of a champion's power arrives late.
data.label: Level curve exponent

data.help: What percentage of its level-60 primaries a champion has at level 1, before rank.
data.label: Level 1 share of final stats

data.help: One entry per star, ★1 first. Multiplies HP, ATK and DEF. ★6 must be 1.0 — it is the authored anchor.
data.label: Star rank multipliers

data.help: Added to the parity chance for each point of ACC over RES, up to the bonus cap.
data.label: Land chance gained per point of accuracy above resistance

data.help: At the default 0.0025 per point this caps out at 28 accuracy over resistance.
data.label: Cap on the accuracy bonus

data.help: Irreducible resist floor of 3%.
data.label: Maximum land chance

data.help: However high resistance climbs, debuffs still land occasionally.
data.label: Minimum land chance

data.help: Probability a debuff sticks when accuracy exactly matches resistance.
data.label: Land chance at ACC = RES

data.help: Each point of RES over ACC costs roughly one percentage point of land chance.
data.label: Land chance lost per point of resistance above accuracy

data.help: Extra resist chance per consecutive hard crowd control on the same unit, Arena only.
data.label: Arena crowd-control resistance

data.help: Random spread applied to every damage roll.
data.label: Damage variance

data.help: K in K/(K+DEF), computed as this × attacker level. 10 gives K=600 at level 60.
data.label: Defence mitigation constant

data.help: Blanket damage reduction when attacking into a stronger element.
data.label: Disadvantage damage penalty

data.help: Buffs and debuffs are capped separately. A full bar rejects further effects of that kind.
data.label: Maximum buffs or debuffs per unit

data.help: Share of the burning unit's max HP dealt to each of its allies when the burn ticks.
data.label: HP Burn splash to allies

data.help: Battles cannot run longer than this.
data.label: Hard turn cap

data.help: Poison is the one status that stacks. The source game allows ten; five suits a smaller roster.
data.label: Maximum poison stacks per unit

data.help: Extra damage on a strong hit.
data.label: Strong hit damage bonus

data.help: Chance of a strong hit when attacking into a weaker element.
data.label: Strong hit chance

data.help: Percentage points of critical rate added when attacking with advantage.
data.label: Strong hit crit bonus

data.help: The tempo constant: TM per tick = SPD × this. 0.07 matches the source game.
data.label: Turn meter gained per speed per tick

data.help: Share of max HP restored to survivors when a wave clears.
data.label: Between-wave heal

data.help: Chance of a weak hit when attacking into a stronger element.
data.label: Weak hit chance

data.help: Damage lost on a weak hit.
data.label: Weak hit damage penalty

data.help: A new account sees every Essence Spring open, rotation or not, for this many days after registering — so a first week is never spent waiting for a Tuesday.
data.label: Springs grace period (days)

data.help: Costs for an Epic champion. `element_*` resolves to the champion’s own element. Rare champions pay the Rare multiplier, Legendary the Legendary one.
data.label: Ascension cost per level

data.help: Multiplies every essence in the ascension table.
data.label: Ascension cost by rarity

data.help: By the released champion’s rarity, scaled by its star rank.
data.label: Silver for releasing a champion

data.help: Used when a stage or shop offer names no distribution of its own.
data.label: Default relic rarity weights

data.help: The source game made removal free in 2025; Mistvale adopts that from the start.
data.label: Free relic removal

data.help: Before the rarity multiplier and the per-level bonus. About 95% of drops are meant to be sold — this is the silver faucet.
data.label: Relic sell base by rank

data.help: Sell value is base × rarity × (1 + this × level), so upgrading is never wholly wasted.
data.label: Relic sell bonus per upgrade level

data.help: Multiplies the rank base.
data.label: Relic sell multiplier by rarity

data.help: How many substats a relic drops with. It gains one at +4, +8, +12 and +16 until it holds four.
data.label: Relic starting substats by rarity

data.help: Silver per attempt at each level 1–16, for a ★6 relic. Lower ranks scale by the rank multipliers. Expected total to +16 at ★6 ≈ 1.8M.
data.label: Relic upgrade cost per level (★6)

data.help: Multiplier applied to the per-level cost, indexed by rank − 1.
data.label: Relic upgrade cost by rank

data.help: Probability each upgrade attempt succeeds. Failures still cost silver — the gamble is the sink.
data.label: Relic upgrade success by level

data.help: What one node of each tier costs. A full fifteen-node build comes to 100 Bronze, 600 Silver and 950 Gold (ECONOMY_BALANCE §7).
data.label: Mastery cost per tier

data.help: Crystals to forget a champion’s masteries. The first reset on each champion is free.
data.label: Mastery reset cost

data.help: A champion cannot ascend past this for its rank — indexed by rank − 1, so ★1 cannot ascend at all and ★6 reaches 6.
data.label: Ascension cap by star rank

data.help: How many automated repeats a player gets each day. Resets at the daily reset hour, not at midnight.
data.label: Multi-battle runs per day

data.help: The largest batch one press may ask for. Smaller than the daily cap on purpose: a batch is a decision the player makes several times a day, not once.
data.label: Multi-battle runs per press

data.help: Informational only — power sorts lists and bands the arena, and is never a combat input.
data.label: Power score weights

data.help: Indexed by the current rank − 1: 1★→2★ costs the first entry. Food champions are consumed on top.
data.label: Rank-up silver fee

data.help: How many tome or duplicate upgrades one skill can take, on top of its published ladder.
data.label: Maximum skill upgrade level

data.help: Tome rarity must match the champion’s (GAME_DESIGN §7).
data.label: Which tome a rarity needs

data.help: Cap is base + perLevel × account level; 18 + 1.85/level gives 20 at level 1 and 129 at 60.
data.label: Energy cap base

data.help: Added to the cap for each account level.
data.label: Energy cap per level

data.help: Flat cost of refilling the bar.
data.label: Crystal cost of a refill

data.help: How long one point of energy takes to return. The source game uses 180.
data.label: Seconds per energy point

data.help: How long after an event shuts its milestones can still be collected. Points stop the moment the window closes — this is only about picking up what was already earned, so somebody who finished a ladder on Sunday evening still has it on Monday morning.
data.label: Event claim grace (days)

data.help: Local hour at which quests, shops and rotations roll over.
data.label: Daily reset hour

data.help: Timezone the reset hour is interpreted in.
data.label: Reset timezone

data.help: Resolved battles and the event logs they carry. Active battles are never pruned at any setting — somebody who left a fight open over a weekend comes back to it. Nothing a player sees depends on this: the prune is about disk.
data.label: Keep finished battles (days)

data.help: The audit trail behind the player inspector and the economy dashboards. Lower it on a box that is filling up; raise it before an investigation.
data.label: Keep the economy log (days)

data.help: A past occurrence’s points and claimed milestones. Dead once the claim grace closes; kept longer so a question about last month’s ladder can still be answered.
data.label: Keep event scores (days)

data.help: How long an expired message stays in the database after it has already vanished from the inbox. Kept a while on purpose: “what did that compensation mail say” is asked after it is gone. Mail with no expiry is never pruned.
data.label: Keep expired mail (days)

data.help: One row per active quest per player per day, so this is the table that grows fastest. A period older than the longest quest period is dead weight — nothing reads it.
data.label: Keep quest instances (days)

data.help: Highest reachable account level.
data.label: Account level cap

data.help: How many champions a new account can hold.
data.label: Starting roster slots

data.help: Items handed over with the starter champion. A new warden should be able to reach the Mistgate on their first evening — ten Faded Sigils is a ×10 on the brood banner, which teaches the mechanic and stocks the first rank-up.
data.label: Welcome grant

data.help: XP needed for level 1 → 2.
data.label: Account XP base

data.help: Multiplier applied per level.
data.label: Account XP growth

data.help: Paid automatically on the day’s first victory in each mode — no claim, because it is a reason to open the game rather than a thing to remember. A mode left out pays nothing. Practice is deliberately absent: it costs nothing and pays nothing by design.
data.label: First win of the day, per mode

data.help: Paid for claiming every chest-counting quest of a period. A period left out of this map simply has no chest — which is how the weekly and monthly currently stand, their pull being the quests themselves. Worth more than any single line, so the last quest of a day is still worth doing.
data.label: Completion chests

data.help: Account level at which the Arena and the Hall of Valor open.
data.label: Arena unlock level

data.help: Account level at which the calendar opens. Nothing is lost by arriving late: a track pays its Nth day on the Nth claim, so somebody who unlocks it on their third evening still starts at day one.
data.label: Login calendar unlock level

data.help: Account level at which champions may be trained — the same level the Proving Grounds opens at, because that is where emblems come from.
data.label: Masteries unlock level

data.help: Account level at which farming without watching becomes available — late enough that a new player has fought a stage by hand first.
data.label: Multi-battle unlock level

data.help: Account level at which the checklist appears. Below it, quests still track — so the first day’s progress is not lost — but nothing is claimable.
data.label: Quests unlock level
